original_test_intent: Qualify DOCA networking performance on the intended HGX/SmartNIC fabric by completing the required NVNetPerf suite and comparing every applicable traffic case with the approved networking configuration thresholds.
original_method: Pin DOCA/NVNetPerf, drivers, firmware, DUT/peer topology, port/direction, NUMA, MTU, link mode, traffic matrix, and metric thresholds; verify isolated peer readiness and clean baseline; run each required suite case with raw timing/throughput/latency/loss and synchronized counters; stop on fabric or host anomalies; reconcile results and restore all traffic/interface state.
manual_activity: Network owner/FAE provisions peers, cabling/optics, isolation, DOCA/NVNetPerf artifacts, and criteria; an operator validates topology and supervises the sustained traffic impact and recovery.
required_inputs: Pinned DOCA SDK, NVNetPerf suite, driver, firmware, and configuration
Link speed/mode, lane, MTU, flow-control, routing/RDMA, message-size, queue, duration, repetition, and concurrency matrix
Per-case throughput, latency, loss, error, variability, and completion thresholds
Network isolation/load limits, baseline-traffic policy, aborts, credential method, and recovery
safety_requirements: Owner approval for endpoints and traffic domain
Never target an unapproved production network
Use verified host identity and secret-safe authentication
Stop on unexpected traffic, congestion, excess loss, link/fabric errors, counter growth, host instability, or thermal/power anomaly
Preserve raw results and do not automatically rerun failed load
agent_execution_scope: Validate suite manifest, topology, criteria, and secure connectivity
Collect complete inventory/baseline and run only approved cases
Preserve per-case/per-direction raw metrics, configs, timestamps, counters, and errors
Compare results to supplied thresholds and check completeness
Do not invent network criteria, bypass host verification, expose credentials, load shared links, retry failures, or issue the formal DUT verdict
engineer_actions: Approve topology, suite scope, load parameters, and network limits
Define quantitative per-case acceptance and allowed background traffic
Own isolation and recovery from link/peer/fabric impact
Review all metrics and decide PASS, FAIL, or BLOCKED

command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use securely authenticated, host-verified sessions and the owner-pinned NVNetPerf suite/configuration; collect untruncated inventory, raw bidirectional case output, and synchronized device/fabric/host counters.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Completion of NVNetPerf suites, networking-criteria comparison, no bundle, and 30/60-minute allocation remain.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Represent each benchmark as a tuple of endpoints, ports, direction, NUMA/CPU, link/MTU/flow control, traffic parameters, and thresholds, with raw metrics and counter deltas.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Turns unspecified networking criteria into an auditable per-case contract and removes insecure/truncated evidence shortcuts.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A DOCA version check or aggregate summary cannot prove the full suite ran on the intended ports/directions or met throughput, latency, loss, and error requirements.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Sustained traffic can congest shared fabric, heat SmartNICs/hosts, disturb peers, and produce misleading results if affinity, routing, MTU, or background traffic is wrong.

project_override_considerations: Do not infer criteria from nominal link rate or a different HGX topology. If NVNetPerf suite membership changes by version, archive the exact manifest and explicitly map every required source coverage item to a result or BLOCKED reason.

Abort/recovery or clean post-load baseline and engineer verdict

review_improvement: Preserves full NVNetPerf coverage while making its topology, criteria, security, raw evidence, shared-network safeguards, and recovery reproducible.
independent_technical_reasoning: Network performance is defined by a configuration, not a standalone number. Throughput can appear low because traffic crossed the wrong port or NUMA node, while a high aggregate can hide one failed direction, packet loss, latency tails, or counter errors. Each NVNetPerf result must therefore carry endpoint and configuration identity and be checked against a case-specific threshold. Secure host verification and untruncated evidence are integral: an unverified remote peer or filtered inventory breaks both provenance and the ability to diagnose a false result. Load isolation is required because the benchmark itself can perturb the network it is measuring.
